svg.aria-label: Architecture map of the testing framework: define, deploy, and run phases
svg.text: 1 · DEFINE — you write this; the builder assembles it into one artifact
one verb per line — eachexpands to builder calls andenables what it needs
the with_*() chain —validates and assemblesthe whole test
your composition code —deploys children in order,exposes typed handles
Scenario §1 — the whole test, described as data
what to deploy — one of three shapes
N identical nodes of one binary
children start in dependency order,readiness-gated; each exposes a typedhandle that test code fetches later
already running — never deployed by the framework
ownership mode — decides available operations and teardown §8
what the run does, and how it is judged
create activity through handles —send jobs · restart nodes · cut the net
duration — the run window; a maximum,
readiness — all / quorum + HTTP or TCP probe
retry — managed spawns retry with backoff
capabilities the test requests up front:
connected straight through to the run —
2 · DEPLOY — the framework starts the system for real
every launched executable —path · env var · cargo build ·download; chained fallbacks,cached, cross-process locked
typed app config renderedinto per-node artifacts forthe container backends
Deployer §10 — one scenario model, three substrates
full node control · the only backend runningapp composition today §10
containers; configs via cfgsync ·restart-level node control
configs via cfgsync · node control only inmanual mode §10
ports · peer view · typed config,written before launch §6persist_dir — pin and reusesnapshot_dir — seed saved statekept on panic / TF_KEEP_LOGS
same provisioning, no Runner —your code sequences start_node ·stop_node · restart_node ·wait_node_ready; nodes stillframework-managed and torn down
drives nodes step-by-step — no Runner, no lifecycle §5
3 · RUN — a fixed lifecycle; test code reaches the system only through the RunContext
started by the deployer — reached via the surfaces on the right
each node: own working dir · ports · typed config §6 §7
left running at teardown · attached = partialcontrol, external = clients only
Grafana / OTLP — externalmonitoring, not test logic
polls app state on a cadence
probe per readiness policy —all nodes or quorum §6
all start concurrently §4 —a panic becomes a clean failure
settle window — starts earlywhen workloads finish early
every one runs — failuresaggregate, no short-circuit
steps 2 and 4 run the workloads and expectations you defined above §4
releases managed resources in reverse acquisition order — attached / external left running
top → bottom = time (define → deploy → run) · solid arrow = builds / owns · dashed arrow = runtime access · §N = the section of this page that unpacks it
dashed box = not owned by the framework
